annotationRationale: The solution reads slopes from general line equations, uses perpendicularity to obtain a=b, and adds the equations supplied by the intersection point to eliminate c.
sourceMethod: Follows the official perpendicular-slopes argument and addition of the substituted equations. Clarifies the vertical-line case so that a=b is justified without assuming b is nonzero.

review.mathCheck: Substitution gives c=a+10=5b−2. Perpendicularity gives a=b, including the horizontal/vertical case, so 4b=12 and c=13, choice E. The unified equations also exclude b=0.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 10 on page 3: relate slopes, substitute the intersection, and eliminate c. The added b=0 discussion correctly closes the official argument's slope exception.
review.annotationCheck: Slope perpendicularity is the assessed skill; extracting slopes and elimination are appropriate support. All cases are adequately handled.
